title: Git and GitHub have different jobs
summary: Git records file history on a computer. GitHub hosts Git repositories and adds pages for collaboration. You can learn local Git without a GitHub account.
introduction: Git records file history on a computer. GitHub hosts Git repositories and adds pages for collaboration. You can learn local Git without a GitHub account. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain git and github have different jobs
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Git records file history on a computer. GitHub hosts Git repositories and adds pages for collaboration. You can learn local Git without a GitHub account.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: These are worked plans, not commands that change a hosted project. You can read many public GitHub pages without an account. Publishing or changing a real project is a separate action on that service.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of GitHub. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
Local computer: edit files and record Git commits
GitHub repository: share selected commits and review proposed changes
blocks.title: Git and GitHub have different jobs

blocks.text: The local and hosted copies are separate places. A local commit does not upload itself to GitHub.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain where a commit made without internet is stored.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not confuse an account on a hosting service with local version history.
For more detail later, use this [GitHub further reading](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started).
